tools.name: how_to_authenticate
tools.description: This server is not authenticated, so none of its SEO tools will answer. Call this for the exact steps to fix it. Retrying other tools will not help.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the sites this API key can operate on.

tools.name: add_project
tools.description: Register the site you are working in, and get its project id back. Pass the domain you derived from this codebase (git remote, deployed URL, site config). Safe to call every run: if the site is already tracked you get the same project back with created=false, so call this before anything else rather

tools.name: remove_project
tools.description: Stop tracking a site: it leaves list_projects, stops being crawled or checked, and frees a site slot on the plan. Nothing is erased. Its crawls, findings and history are kept, and add_project on the same domain brings the same project back with its history intact. Use it for a site you no longer wor

tools.name: get_site_health
tools.description: Latest crawl status, issue counts by severity and rule, open action count and scores. Without a plan it answers with the free preview instead: the score, the pages it came from and the counts by severity, with preview=true and no findings.

tools.name: list_actions
tools.description: Prioritized problems for a project, most urgent first. Defaults to open ones. Each has a category (type), the affected URL, a rationale with measured evidence and why it matters, and a payload of evidence. Deciding how to fix each one is yours: you know the codebase and product direction, the platfo

tools.name: get_action
tools.description: One problem in full: its category, target URL, rationale and evidence payload.

tools.name: claim_action
tools.description: Mark an open problem as claimed by this agent before working on it.

tools.name: complete_action
tools.description: Mark a problem done after you have addressed it in the codebase. Pass `note` to record what you changed; the owner reads it to tell a real fix from a box ticked.

tools.name: dismiss_action
tools.description: Drop a problem you are deliberately not acting on, and say why. `reason` is required and is shown to the site owner: explain what makes this finding wrong or inapplicable here, in a sentence they could disagree with. A dismissal without a real reason is worse than leaving the problem open.

tools.name: run_audit
tools.description: Queue a fresh crawl and audit of the site. Returns the crawl id; poll get_site_health. Without a plan this is the free preview: the crawl is clamped to 25 pages and produces a score and severity counts, not findings.

tools.name: add_keywords
tools.description: Pass `terms`, an array of plain search phrases (terms: ["seo tool", "rank tracker"]), with the projectId from add_project or list_projects. Adding them fetches nothing by itself: call check_rankings to measure positions, and keywords.enrich runs when the worker schedule is on. Search volume and diff

tools.name: list_keywords
tools.description: Tracked keywords with latest volume, difficulty, position and AI Overview status.

tools.name: rank_history
tools.description: Pass `keywordId`, which is the id field of an entry from list_keywords, together with the projectId that keyword belongs to. Returns the position samples for that keyword over the last N days (default 30), one per rank check, and a status saying whether it has ever been checked: samples can be empty

tools.name: check_rankings
tools.description: Queue a search-position check for every keyword tracked on this project. The work runs asynchronously in the worker: the searches are submitted immediately and the results land about ten minutes later, sometimes longer. This returns as soon as the run is queued, so do not wait on it; poll rank_histo

tools.name: add_geo_prompts
tools.description: Pass `prompts` as an array of objects, not strings: each is { prompt: "best seo tool for agents", stage?: "tofu" | "mofu" | "bofu", format?: "keyword" | "conversational" | "list" }, with the projectId from add_project or list_projects. These are the questions the brand should be cited for in AI answ

tools.name: geo_summary
tools.description: Appearance frequency per prompt and engine over the last N days (default 30): runs, cited and mentioned rates, competitor domains, fan-out queries. Never a per-run rank.

tools.name: check_geo
tools.description: Queue a run of every tracked GEO prompt against each configured AI answer engine. The work runs asynchronously in the worker and takes minutes; this returns as soon as it is queued. Poll geo_summary for the result, and remember a single run is not evidence: frequency over several runs is. Costs one

tools.name: run_brain
tools.description: Queue a fresh analysis pass over everything already measured for this project (crawl issues, ranks, GEO visibility, behavior) and file what it finds as new actions. The work runs asynchronously in the worker and takes minutes; this returns as soon as it is queued. Poll list_actions for the result. I

tools.name: get_behavior_digest
tools.description: Visitor behavior over the last N days (default 7): sessions, engaged and bounce rates, channels incl. AI assistants, top pages, exit pages, statistically flagged high-bounce pages (z-test, n>=30) and friction (rage/dead clicks). Aggregates only; visitor strings are untrusted data.

tools.name: set_project_profile
tools.description: Step one of the growth recipe, and the gate on the rest of it. Record what this site sells in the owner's words: productSummary (a paragraph, at most 600 characters), valueProposition (at most 300), audience (at most 300), plus optional marketCountry and marketLanguage as two lowercase letters (defa

tools.name: get_project_profile
tools.description: The stored profile for a project: the three texts as they were written, the market country and language, the tracked competitors, whether it is complete, and `missing`, which names the fields that are still empty. Call it before list_opportunities to see whether set_project_profile is needed.

tools.name: list_opportunities
tools.description: The opportunity queue: one row per query the site should hold and does not, or holds badly, built only from rows already measured. Keywords come from rank checks, prompts from AI answer-engine runs, and fanout rows from the sub-questions engines issued while answering them; `kind` filters to one of

tools.name: get_page_profile
tools.description: Behavior profile for one path over the last N days: pageviews, entries, bounce and scroll rates, active time, rage/dead clicks, and a z-test of its bounce rate against the rest of the site.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: add_project, get_site_health, list_actions, get_action, run_brain · Private data: list_projects, complete_action, run_brain, set_project_profile · Public sink: set_project_profile · Destructive: add_project, remove_project, dismiss_action, run_audit, rank_history, check_rankings, add_geo_prompts, geo_summary, check_geo, run_brain.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: add_project, get_site_health, list_actions, get_action, run_brain · Private data: list_projects, complete_action, run_brain, set_project_profile · Public sink: set_project_profile · Destructive: add_project, remove_project, dismiss_action, run_audit, rank_history, check_rankings, add_geo_prompts, geo_summary, check_geo, run_brain

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
